assumptions: Destination enum derived from the installed fleet roster (14 *-fleet skills) minus `fleet-command` (a conductor over fleets, never a destination for an issue) and `issue-fleet` itself (the producer of the route; routing an issue to the router is a cycle), yielding 12 destinations. The brief required at minimum the six in the vendored enum plus docs/security/perf/craft; the roster additionally supplied `bug` and `ideate`.

`ideate` was INCLUDED as a destination although `ideate-fleet` files nothing and sits at the head of the spine rather than consuming a queue. Rationale: an open-ended 'we should explore X' issue has a plausible home there, and omitting a roster member silently is the failure mode this issue is about. A reviewer who disagrees should drop it from DESTINATIONS in scripts/lib/route-labels.mjs and update the count assertion in ts/test/route-labels.test.ts.

`route:unroutable` was added as a 13th label beyond the 12 destinations. The issue's third acceptance bullet requires an unroutable issue be reported as unroutable rather than silently dropped, and the absence of a route label cannot carry that meaning because it already means 'not yet triaged'.

Canary's side of the contract was built as `scripts/lib/*.mjs` + `scripts/*.mjs` rather than a new `canary` CLI subcommand, following the `backfill-type-labels.mjs` / `type-label-infer.mjs` precedent (#880). A new ts/src CLI surface would engage the dead-exports, perf-complexity, and arch-allowance ratchets for a repo-governance tool with no product-runtime consumer.

A multi-route issue is classified as `conflicted` and is never auto-resolved. The issue did not specify this case; resolving it silently would corrupt the downstream queue with an answer nobody chose.
Label colour BFD4F2 was chosen to match the existing `fleet:claimed` label, since the brief specified mirroring that pattern.
`ensure-labels` defaults to a dry run and only ever CREATES labels; no delete or edit path exists, so a mis-run cannot destroy triage state.
The 13 labels were created on the live tracker as part of this lane, per the brief's instruction to create them and list them auditably.

acceptance.route-persists-beyond-session: A route is recorded as a GitHub label on the issue itself, readable by any later session or tool.
acceptance.denominator-report: `node scripts/route-queue.mjs report [--json]` prints routed / unroutable / untriaged / conflicted over an examined count, and names every issue in each population.
acceptance.degrades-honestly: Zero examined exits 3 (ABSTENTION, never a pass); a gh failure exits 2 so an unreadable tracker is not reported as an empty one; the four populations sum to the denominator so an issue cannot be silently dropped.

gates: check-deps (repo root): pass, 212 modules across 11 layers
verification.planted-positive: Rewiring `report` to pass `--label` to `gh issue list` turned 3 tests red, confirming the label-filter assertions are not vacuous.
